title: Update example in step_dummy() docs to omit grep()
description:
Currently following the example in the `step_dummy()` docs requires knowing what `grep()` does and what `^` means in a regex. It's possible to accomplish the same outcome with `select(starts_with())` without adding a package dependency, so at a minimum I would suggest replacing

https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/blob/394b4019443c623441d432d4bfdfbfa1f5d88418/R/dummy.R#L98-L99

with

```r
unique(okc$diet) %>% sort()
dummy_data %>%
  select(starts_with("diet")) %>%
  names() 
```

Further reorganizing the full example like the following might be even more effective for communicating the difference between dummy coding and one-hot encoding.

``` r
suppressMessages(library(recipes))
library(modeldata)

data(okc)
okc <- okc[complete.cases(okc),]

rec <- recipe(~ diet + age + height, data = okc)

# Original data: diet has 18 levels

length(unique(okc$diet))
#> [1] 18

unique(okc$diet) %>% sort()
#>  [1] "anything"            "halal"               "kosher"             
#>  [4] "mostly anything"     "mostly halal"        "mostly kosher"      
#>  [7] "mostly other"        "mostly vegan"        "mostly vegetarian"  
#> [10] "other"               "strictly anything"   "strictly halal"     
#> [13] "strictly kosher"     "strictly other"      "strictly vegan"     
#> [16] "strictly vegetarian" "vegan"               "vegetarian"

# Dummy coding: 17 dummy variables

dummies <- rec %>% 
  step_dummy(diet) %>%
  prep(training = okc)

dummy_data <- bake(dummies, new_data = NULL)

dummy_data %>%
  select(starts_with("diet")) %>%
  names() # level anything is the reference level
#>  [1] "diet_halal"               "diet_kosher"             
#>  [3] "diet_mostly.anything"     "diet_mostly.halal"       
#>  [5] "diet_mostly.kosher"       "diet_mostly.other"       
#>  [7] "diet_mostly.vegan"        "diet_mostly.vegetarian"  
#>  [9] "diet_other"               "diet_strictly.anything"  
#> [11] "diet_strictly.halal"      "diet_strictly.kosher"    
#> [13] "diet_strictly.other"      "diet_strictly.vegan"     
#> [15] "diet_strictly.vegetarian" "diet_vegan"              
#> [17] "diet_vegetarian"

# One hot encoding: 18 dummy variables 
# Using the `one_hot` option

dummies_one_hot <- rec %>% 
  step_dummy(diet, one_hot = TRUE) %>%
  prep(training = okc)

dummy_data_one_hot <- bake(dummies_one_hot, new_data = NULL)

dummy_data_one_hot %>%
  select(starts_with("diet")) %>%
  names() # no reference level
#>  [1] "diet_anything"            "diet_halal"              
#>  [3] "diet_kosher"              "diet_mostly.anything"    
#>  [5] "diet_mostly.halal"        "diet_mostly.kosher"      
#>  [7] "diet_mostly.other"        "diet_mostly.vegan"       
#>  [9] "diet_mostly.vegetarian"   "diet_other"              
#> [11] "diet_strictly.anything"   "diet_strictly.halal"     
#> [13] "diet_strictly.kosher"     "diet_strictly.other"     
#> [15] "diet_strictly.vegan"      "diet_strictly.vegetarian"
#> [17] "diet_vegan"               "diet_vegetarian"

# Tidy recipe information

tidy(dummies, number = 1)
#> # A tibble: 18 x 3
#>    terms columns             id         
#>    <chr> <chr>               <chr>      
#>  1 diet  anything            dummy_ek6Im
#>  2 diet  halal               dummy_ek6Im
#>  3 diet  kosher              dummy_ek6Im
#>  4 diet  mostly anything     dummy_ek6Im
#>  5 diet  mostly halal        dummy_ek6Im
#>  6 diet  mostly kosher       dummy_ek6Im
#>  7 diet  mostly other        dummy_ek6Im
#>  8 diet  mostly vegan        dummy_ek6Im
#>  9 diet  mostly vegetarian   dummy_ek6Im
#> 10 diet  other               dummy_ek6Im
#> 11 diet  strictly anything   dummy_ek6Im
#> 12 diet  strictly halal      dummy_ek6Im
#> 13 diet  strictly kosher     dummy_ek6Im
#> 14 diet  strictly other      dummy_ek6Im
#> 15 diet  strictly vegan      dummy_ek6Im
#> 16 diet  strictly vegetarian dummy_ek6Im
#> 17 diet  vegan               dummy_ek6Im
#> 18 diet  vegetarian          dummy_ek6Im

tidy(dummies_one_hot, number = 1)
#> # A tibble: 18 x 3

title: Harmonize recipe steps to use snake-case and common-text-first format
description:
This suggestion is in relation to https://github.com/tidymodels/recipes/pull/555#discussion_r506441161. I suggested naming `step_lmimpute()` to `step_impute_lm()`, with the possibility of future consolidation of the nomenclature for the imputation steps to use snake-case and the tidy format of placing common text first, to benefit from tab-autocompletion and fuzzy-narrowing.

I'd be happy to spin up a PR draft to soft-deprecate the existing imputation steps using `lifecycle`, if you'd like.

title: If a predictor is of type factor beforehand and then step_novel and step_dummy is applied, prediction fails on observation with novel factor level.
description:
Hi,
I ran into inconsistent behavior with step_novel and step_dummy depending on if the predictor was a factor or character vector before prep/bake.
If the predictor was character vector and step_novel and step_dummy is applied as preprocessor, it works correctly on test data with new level(s) that was not present in train data.
But if the predictor was of type factor already before prep/bake and step_novel and step_dummy is applied, prediction fails on test data observation with new level.
I am not sure why that is the case. Any help in understanding this behavior would be greatly appreciated.

title: Recipes eats too much RAM
description:
Hello,

Thank you for the great package!

The "recipes" eases and automates the data preprocessing in a very high degree. Unfortunately, it comes with the costs of high RAM usage. 

In the example bellow, manually preprocessed data and model built via "caret" takes up to 201 MB whereas doing the same procedures via "recipes" takes up to 665 MB. In practice, where the work is with much bigger datasets (with the dimensions 50 000 x 500) and many more preprocessing steps, the difference is not 3-fold but already a 10-fold (solely "caret" model takes 500 MB of RAM whereas the equivalent "recipes" model takes about 5 GB). Unfortunately, the following RAM issue prevents us to use the "recipes" in the production environment where we host tens of different model APIs. 

I will be grateful to hear the solutions for the RAM issue.


```
library(carData)
library(caret)
library(forcats)

data(MplsStops)
df <- MplsStops

##Preprocesing
for(i in 1:ncol(df)) {
  if(is.factor(df[, i])) {
    levels(MplsStops[,i]) <- make.names(levels(MplsStops[,i]))
    df[, i] <- fct_explicit_na(MplsStops[, i], na_level = "NA_value")
  }
}

##Train caret model
the_control <- trainControl(
  method = 'none',
  summaryFunction = twoClassSummary,
  classProbs = TRUE,
  savePredictions = FALSE
)

fit <- train(problem ~ .,
             data = df[, !colnames(df) %in% c('idNum', 'date')],
             method = 'ranger',
             metric = 'ROC',
             tuneGrid = data.frame(mtry = 4, splitrule = 'gini', min.node.size = 1),
             trControl = the_control
             )

m1 <- pryr::mem_used()
m1 <- pryr::mem_used()


##Preprocessing and training with recipes
rm(fit, df)
.rs.restartR() #Restart the R session now
df <- MplsStops

library(caret)
library(recipes)
rec <- recipe(problem ~ ., data = df) %>%
  update_role(idNum, date, new_role = 'non_predictor') %>%
  step_unknown(all_nominal(), -all_outcomes(), new_level = 'NA_value')

fit <- train(rec,
             data = df,
             method = 'ranger',
             metric = 'ROC',
             tuneGrid = data.frame(mtry = 4, splitrule = 'gini', min.node.size = 1),
             trControl = the_control
)

m2 <- pryr::mem_used()
```

title: Should keyword arguments in `step_*()` be preceded by a dot?
description:
Since it's impossible to add/modify variables with the same names as `step_mutate()`'s keyword arguments (e.g., `id`) inside `step_mutate()`, is it more appropriate to change the arguments' names to be preceded by a dot (e.g., `.id`) so that it is less likely to collide with variable names?

For example, suppose I want to create a variable called `id` that stores the row number of each observation for the `iris` data set, this won't work:

``` r
library(recipes)
#> Loading required package: dplyr
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'dplyr'
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     filter, lag
#> The following objects are masked from 'package:base':
#> 
#>     intersect, setdiff, setequal, union
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'recipes'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     step
library(magrittr)
data(iris)

iris %>%
  recipe() %>%
  step_mutate(id = 1:nrow(iris)) %>%
  prep() %>%
  bake(new_data = NULL) %>%
  select(id)
#> Error: Can't subset columns that don't exist.
#> x Column `id` doesn't exist.
```

<sup>Created on 2021-01-27 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v0.3.0)</sup>

Similarly, it's also not possible to add/modify variables using names like `role`, `train`, `inputs`, `skip`.

If changing the names of the keyword arguments is not feasible, there should perhaps be a workaround.

title: Challenges using `all_nominal()` and `all_numeric()`
description:
We have lots of examples of folks having trouble with `all_nominal()` and `all_numeric()` when they accidentally select outcomes or other non-predictors. Mine talked about running into this during teaching, and here is [one example of many from the general user base](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/65180483/trying-to-predict-the-probability-of-a-binary-variable-being-equal-to-1-using-ti/65221996#65221996). A significant challenge is that because of how/when these steps are evaluated, the error message is often opaque.

What would be a good way to reduce this friction?

- Should `all_nominal()` and `all_numeric()` only select predictors?
- Should these be replaced by new selectors like `all_nominal_preds()` and `all_numeric_preds()`?
- Some recipe steps are more prone to this problem, like `step_dummy()`. Protections at the step level?
- Something else?

title: Suggestion: add a keep_vars arguments (for some steps)
description:
I am thinking in particular on multivariate steps such as pca or ica.
Sometimes, I am interested in feature engineering so that I would like to generate PCA plus keep source variables.
As PCA allows adding prefix such as "PCA_", one may still manipulate source variables with a `-starts_with("PCA")`.
Same for `embed` package.

I expected `lag_1_val` in the assessment set to pull from the analysis set and thus be 50, which didn't happen.

This is perhaps a big change to `step_lag`, but it seems essential for using this step in almost any real-world problem.

A tricky aspect to also consider is, what if I had set `skip` to be 1 or more? How could that be handled appropriately in `step_lag`? If `skip = 1`, the first obs in the assessment set would need to draw from that skipped observation, which would not normally be accessible to the recipe.

This is also related to the (long) discussion in https://github.com/tidymodels/rsample/issues/42, and the notion that skips can be implied by the lagging of features. Time makes everything harder!
